name: Probability
description: Chance, outcomes, random variables and the bell curve, taught at the Kepler outpost.
about: Probability realm ("Probability"): outcomes, chances, random variables and the normal curve, for an adult who has finished Foundations and nothing more. Same Kepler outpost, where nothing is certain any more and Mira keeps the odds board. The concept plan is docs/PROB-PLAN.md.

chapters.name: Chance and outcomes
chapters.blurb: Outcomes, equally likely chances, long-run frequency, complements and the addition rule.

chapters.name: Conditions and independence

sector.name: Sorting Shed

chapters.name: Updating and payoffs

chapters.name: Rare events and waiting times

chapters.name: The normal curve

mentor.name: Mira
mentor.opening: I’m Mira. Nothing here is certain any more, and we have to {purpose}. Your task is “{title}.” {brief} The idea we need: {topic}.
mentor.closing: You already have what this needs from Foundations, and the only new habit is to turn a guess into a number. I’ll go through the worked example with you, and the guided steps are there whenever you want them.

copy.homeTitle:
Nothing here is certain.
Learn to measure chance.
copy.firstVisit: Welcome back. The supply runs have started, and some arrive late, some crates crack and some seeds never sprout. We start with a bag of tokens and one fraction; everything you need you learned in Foundations.
copy.allDone: You did it. Every station runs on numbers, not hunches, and you can say how likely anything here is. Data and inference turns this round and asks what real samples tell us.
copy.chaptersNote: Seven chapters. Learn every concept in a chapter to unlock a landmark for the outpost. Practice missions are optional.

skills.title: The skill tree
skills.text: Follow the prerequisite branches from outcomes to the normal curve. Each mission you finish opens the ideas that are built on it.

visual.title: The concept bench
visual.text: Pick any mission, change its numbers and predict the result before you check it. Nothing here affects your progress, and it all works offline.

help.title: Chance, measured.
help.intro: Probability starts where Foundations ends, with fractions, decimals and percent. It teaches outcomes, the rules for combining chances, random variables and the normal curve. Every new word and symbol is explained before you are asked to use it, with a worked example first.
help.answers: A probability is a fraction in lowest terms, a decimal rounded as the mission says, or a count; a yes or no question takes 1 or 0.
